chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Ibrahim, who said:

I asked him about prayer on a ship. He said: 'He prays while sitting if he is unable to stand on the ship, and he does not pray on the ship while he is able to [pray] on the shore.' And he said: 'He prays on the ship, turning his face towards the Qibla, then he prays however the ship turns.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer on a moving ship if they cannot stand?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the jurisprudential principle of *rukhsa* (concession) for travelers, prioritizing ease when physical stability is compromised by the ship's motion. It clarifies that while facing the Qibla is the ideal orientation, the validity of the prayer is maintained even if the body rotates with the vessel, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical adaptability in worship. This ruling underscores the balance between maintaining ritual integrity and accommodating the physical realities of sea travel.
